fut.text: Sorin Markov's part in Future Sight is a small but pivotal one: he releases Ugin from the hedron cocoon that had held him.
It follows the moment Nissa breaks the central hedron in the Eye of Ugin and frees the Eldrazi Titans.

roe.text: Sorin Markov first appears in the Rise of the Eldrazi story as one of three planeswalkers who decided to rid the Multiverse of the Eldrazi, joining Ugin and Nahiri. When the Eldrazi could not simply be destroyed, Sorin lured them in, Ugin bound them with colorless magic, and Nahiri's hedron network formed the bars of their prison on Zendikar.

The three sealed the Eye of Ugin with a lock that needed three planeswalker sparks and Ugin's breath, and then they disbanded, with Sorin and Ugin leaving and Nahiri staying behind to guard the prison. Sorin and Ugin promised to come if Nahiri ever signaled, but when vampires built a shrine that destabilized the prison, her calls for help went unanswered and she restored it alone.

Much later, Sorin returned to Zendikar and met Nissa, who guided him toward Akoum while he freed Anowon from the brood. Aboard ship Sorin revealed that he was a planeswalker and that the titans lay bound beneath Akoum, and that it was his duty to keep them sealed. When Nissa pushed him to admit he was a vampire and the cause of the vanishings, he had little to say in his own defense.

At the Eye of Ugin, Nissa shattered the central hedron and dissolved the binding enchantment, releasing the titans despite Sorin's intent to reseal the prison. Sorin washed his hands of her and abandoned the plane, and Nissa vowed before the Joraga Council to find him and bring him back.

isd.text: Sorin Markov's story on Innistrad begins with his grandfather Edgar Markov, who inflicted vampirism on him and so awakened his latent planeswalker spark. Sorin left the plane, and returned after centuries to find vampires pushing humanity toward extinction.

Edgar dismissed his concerns, so Sorin acted on his own: he created the archangel Avacyn to safeguard humanity and forged the Helvault from a piece of Innistrad's silver moon. Avacyn and her angels slew vampires with holy fervor, and Sorin's kin branded him a traitor.

Nahiri then found him at the Helvault site, angry that her call for help had gone unanswered, and when she attacked, Avacyn joined the fight. Sorin ended the battle by sealing Nahiri inside the Helvault.
Years later Sorin mustered the surviving Markov vampires to retake Edgar's manor.

dka.text: Sorin Markov's Dark Ascension story retells his past: the demon Shilgengar preyed on Edgar's ambition, and Edgar's blood experiment ended with Sorin made a vampire, his planeswalker spark igniting from the trauma. Seeing vampires dwindle the human villages, Sorin created the angel Avacyn and tasked her with protecting Innistrad, though most vampires reviled him as a traitor.
He returns to find vampires killing at will, werewolves preying on cathars and ghouls besieging Thraben, and he draws his sword. Sorin laments that only the shadow of his creation remains.

avr.text: In Avacyn Restored, Sorin Markov is the creator behind the angel at the center of the story: he made the archangel Avacyn to safeguard humanity, and fashioned the Helvault from a chunk of the silver moon so she could seal away threats. Avacyn battled demons such as Ormendahl for about a thousand years.

Long before, Nahiri had come seeking Sorin's aid, and provoked, he had Avacyn imprison her in the Helvault. With the Helvault sundered, she was freed and returned to a ravaged Zendikar, where she swore vengeance on Sorin.
She destroyed Markov Manor, and Sorin found it in ruins and sought help from Olivia Voldaren. Nahiri wounded him, encased him in stone at the manor and planeswalked away.

ktk.text: Sorin Markov arrives on Tarkir in Khans of Tarkir searching for the spirit dragon Ugin, led by an oracle's visions toward a dragon-head peak. He is troubled by Nahiri's silence and Ugin's absence while the Eldrazi titans rampage on Zendikar.
Sorin feeds on a sentry, then kills two Temur warriors who mistake him for a Sultai demon-spawn and raises them as vampire thralls. He dominates a survivor to serve as his guide to Ugin.

The guide leads him to a chasm where only huge bones lie, and Sorin refuses to believe it is Ugin until he descends and finds Ugin's skull in the ice. He fears Zendikar and then Innistrad will be consumed, and says they are all doomed.

The ktk-era story also looks back at Sorin with Nahiri on a dying world, where he admits they are not winning against the creatures. They flee to a kor settlement in Akoum on Zendikar, where Ugin appears and proposes imprisoning the three titans on a single plane.

When the titans arrive, Ugin and Sorin fight their brood, and the three planeswalkers focus their power in the Eye of Ugin, shifting every hedron into place and leaving the three Eldrazi petrified over Akoum.

dtk.text: In Dragons of Tarkir, Sorin Markov returns to Tarkir uneasy beneath the sun, still searching for Ugin and guided only by an oracle's vague impressions. A party of Atarka warriors mistakes him for a Silumgar death-spawn, so he enthralls one as a guide and learns that the dragons now rule and that Ugin dwells in the Haven.

He finds a hedron cocoon in a chasm and wonders whether Nahiri was there before him, then drains the thrall and uses blood magic to unmake the cocoon, freeing Ugin. Ugin explains that he was attacked by Bolas, who used his own dragons against him.

Sorin tells him that over a thousand years have passed and the Eldrazi have escaped their prison, partly through Nissa's choice. Ugin asks after Nahiri and insists all three of them must work together, so Sorin agrees to find her and meet Ugin at the Eye as he planeswalks away.

soi.text: Sorin Markov is the person everyone in Shadows over Innistrad is looking for or running from. Jace says he is searching for Sorin, who helped trap the Eldrazi on Zendikar, while Liliana, who remembers Sorin testing her in battle and judging her too weak, warns him not to go because Sorin is ancient, ruthless and powerful.

Sorin himself is hunting for Nahiri, who has vowed to take everything from him. He walks through Olivia Voldaren's masked ballroom, cuts down five of her vampires, and tells her he has come for her help, since his grandfather's manor is in ruins.

Olivia agrees to help on the condition that he first helps her, and the price is Avacyn. Sorin finds Avacyn in Thraben Cathedral and reveals he is her creator, but she condemns him as the greatest evil of the world and sends her angels against him.

Sorin destroys the angels one by one, but Avacyn, seeing a monster, can finally hurt him and drives her spear through his chest. He drives her down into the cellar where she was made, offers to remake her, and when she refuses, destroys her by performing the ritual in reverse.

emn.text: Sorin Markov's old debt to Nahiri comes due in Eldritch Moon. She confronts him, saying she resealed the Eldrazi prison alone after neither he nor Ugin answered her signal, but Sorin shows no concern and says he took her under his wing and owes her nothing. When she demands he return with her to Zendikar, he disarms her and hurls her into the Helvault.

Free again, Nahiri summons Emrakul to Innistrad to take revenge on Sorin. Meanwhile Sorin destroys the corrupted Avacyn in Thraben Cathedral to win Olivia's help, and Emrakul arrives as he realizes he played into Nahiri's plan.

Sorin and Olivia lead the Voldaren vampire army off to meet Nahiri, who tells him she brought Emrakul to his doorstep and is done being a warden. Sorin's blade stabs her and he drinks her blood, but she drives stone tusks into him and traps him in a stone cocoon before planeswalking away.
Olivia declares their bargain fulfilled, takes his sword and leaves him in stone, while Sorin watches Emrakul drift toward Thraben.

cmr.text: In Commander Legends, Sorin Markov speaks over the entombed Ugin, telling him that the corpses of worlds will join him in the tomb.

mid.text: Sorin Markov spends Midnight Hunt guarding a secret. Sensing a plot, he races to his grandfather's resting-crypt, and the spirit of Dennick Betzold tells Arlinn's group that the Moonsilver Key was given to Sorin.

Brooding in Markov Manor, Sorin refuses to give up the Key and strikes Arlinn when Avacyn is mentioned, until Sigarda appears and stops him. While Sigarda fights Sorin, Arlinn and Teferi recover the Key from the Markov catacombs.

vow.text: Sorin Markov refuses at first to give up the key in Crimson Vow, saying he has sacrificed enough, and slashes Arlinn's arm when she brings up Avacyn. Sigarda blocks his blow so the others can find the key in his chambers.

Arlinn argues that the endless night will starve the vampires too, so Sorin learns that Edgar's coffin has been stolen and that Olivia Voldaren plans to marry him and rule all of Innistrad. At the wedding Sorin charges at Olivia but is bound in Blessed Silver chains, while Edgar wakes and dismisses his warnings.

Sorin works out that Olivia means to control all the angels by drinking Sigarda's blood, cuts his chains with blood magic and fights her until Sigarda is freed. He then follows Edgar to the sanguitorium to make him see he is being used, but Edgar throws him into a great pit.

Lying in a pit of blood, Sorin reflects on Nahiri, Avacyn and his grandfather's betrayal, then drinks the blood to heal. He climbs out, duels Edgar and defeats him, and then spares his life, telling him to get out of his sight.

m12.text: Sorin Markov joined the planeswalker lineup of Magic 2012, taking the place of Liliana alongside Gideon.
The set's flavor shows Sorin ramming his blade into a would-be swordsman's heart and drawing the victim's blood up the blade into himself.
